newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. spot power slides along with BPA drop.
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. spot power slides along with BPA drop.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the western U.S. slid Monday in tandem with Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) decrease of its daily peak-hour prices, industry sources said.
"We saw prices down $1.50 at Palo Verde (PV), down 50 cents at COB (California-Oregon Border), and flat at Mid-C (Mid-Columbia)," said one Houston trader.
Market participants noted continual downward pressure on western physical prices since last week on persistent cool weather in much of the U.S. and declining demand for air-conditioning.

Reflecting the bearish tenor in the market, BPA early today lowered Tuesday's power prices to $17.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) during hours 0700-1200 and 2200-2300 PDT, and $19.00 during hours 1300-2100 PDT, down one dollar from Friday's values for Monday's heavy load hours.
The federal power marketing agency kept its daily off-peak price unchanged for Tuesday at $13.00.
COB prices for peak, firm delivery on Tuesday were quoted at $14.00-$15.50, compared with Friday's $15.00 for Monday.
October COB was assessed at $15.45-$15.75, a tighter range than Friday's $15.25-$15.75.
At Mid-C, electricity for next-day peak, firm delivery was pegged at $13.25-$14.00, and October delivery $15.20-$15.50.
Down at the PV delivery near Phoenix, Ariz., firm, peak prices for Tuesday were discussed at $17.50-$18.50, much lower than Friday's $19.00-$20.00 range.
October PV values were talked between $15.60 and $15.90, down from a quote $15.75-$16.25 on Friday.
